speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg started and how long it has been there? Also, have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever or fatigue accompanying it?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent uveitis, does the lesion have a raised, violaceous border or appear as a purpuric nodule? I am also interested in knowing if you have experienced any joint pain or abdominal symptoms recently that might suggest active inflammatory bowel disease.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of an insect bite triggering a painful, necrotic ulcer with violaceous borders in a patient with Crohn's disease is classic for Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I will request imaging to confirm the clinical appearance and rule out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent travel to Wisconsin, have you noticed any other skin lesions, particularly ring-shaped rashes, or experienced joint pain in your large joints? I want to rule out Lyme disease or other travel-related infections that could mimic this presentation.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of pathergy following an insect bite and the patient's underlying Crohn's disease, Pyoderma Gangrenosum is the most likely diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
